svg.title: DartClaw in its surroundings
svg.desc: C4 context view. DartClaw is one system. Around it: the operator and MCP clients who call its HTTP server, channel users who reach it through messaging platforms and their sidecars, the provider binaries it spawns and the model APIs behind them, PostgreSQL, the container runtime, git remotes, web and search services, embedding sources and outbound MCP servers.

g.text: Hover a box for what it is and how it connects; its edges light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: One host process serves people over HTTP and chat, and drives provider binaries and sidecars as child processes.

g.text: Channel users · people chatting with the agent on WhatsApp, Signal, Google Chat or Slack
They reach DartClaw only through the platform and its adapter; allowlists and governance apply per channel.
Operator · the one administrator per instance, in a browser or at the CLI
Connected CLI commands use the same HTTP API; a standalone workflow run needs no server.
MCP clients · named MCP clients, such as context-engine clients, calling /mcp with a bearer token
A named client's profile is exactly context_research, kg_query and kg_timeline; guards and audit run on every dispatch.
DartClaw · one Dart host process: the control plane, fully trusted
It owns state, policy and orchestration; the provider binaries and sidecars are its child processes.
web UI, REST API, /mcp, four channel adapters
guard chain, governance, container posture, audit
Messaging platforms · WhatsApp, Signal, Google Chat and Slack
Each adapter normalizes its payload into one ChannelMessage at ingress; Google Chat and Slack need no sidecar.
Channel sidecars · GOWA (WhatsApp) and signal-cli (Signal), spawned and restarted by the host
GOWA posts webhooks and takes REST calls; signal-cli runs an HTTP daemon, SSE in and JSON-RPC out. Restarts back off, at most 5 attempts.
docker or podman · the container runtime CLI that ContainerManager drives
Optional: an unset container.enabled isolates only if a runtime is detected; native Windows has no container isolation.
PostgreSQL 14+ · tasks, runs, traces, events, knowledge-graph facts and search projections; native or managed
pgvector is needed only for hybrid search; a standalone workflow run needs no database.
Embedding sources · a local EmbeddingGemma model downloaded from Hugging Face, or an explicitly configured endpoint
Optional: a provider failure leaves the lexical search projection current and reports a structured degradation.
Provider binaries · claude, codex and configured ACP agents, spawned as child processes by the host
Container or host for claude and codex, host only for ACP; the wire formats are in Control Protocol.
Provider APIs · the model services behind the provider binaries
Host executions reach them with a provider-scoped credential; container executions reach one pinned upstream through HostGateway.
Git remotes · remotes of external projects: the git CLI clones, fetches and pushes, the GitHub REST API opens pull requests
Used only for external projects; git credentials are host-held (Security Architecture).
Web and webhooks · pages fetched by web_fetch, the Brave and Tavily search APIs, and the URL a scheduled job posts its result to
NetworkGuard evaluates web_fetch; a job webhook is a JSON POST with a 10 s timeout.
Outbound MCP · external MCP servers configured under mcp_servers
OutboundMcpPool pools connections; every call passes the egress guard and is audited before the server is contacted.
